page: Google Cloud Platform m4-ultramem-112 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance engineered for workloads demanding extensive memory capacities relative to processor resources. Powered by the x86_64 architecture, this instance provides 112 dedicated vCPUs alongside 2976.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 26.57 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or hardware accelerators such as GPUs, relying instead on network-attached block storage solutions for persistent data needs.

From an infrastructure and cost efficiency standpoint, the m4-ultramem-112 targets enterprise deployments where high memory-to-vCPU ratios reduce the overhead of multi-node horizontal scaling. By consolidating very large working datasets onto a single virtual system, organizations can optimize operational complexity and per-node licensing overheads. However, the architectural absence of bundled local NVMe storage and complementary public IPv4 addresses requires relying on external cloud storage volumes and virtual network routing, which should be accounted for during system provisioning.

Given its substantial 2976.0 GB memory footprint and 112 dedicated compute cores, the m4-ultramem-112 is tailored for ultra-high-density memory architectures. Primary workload fits include enterprise-scale in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, massive in-memory caching systems, large transactional relational database servers, and extensive in-memory extract-transform-load (ETL) processing jobs.
description: Google Cloud Platform m4-ultramem-112 is an enterprise memory-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture, offering 112 dedicated vCPUs and 2976.0 GB of system memory. Providing 26.57 GB of RAM per vCPU, this configuration facilitates large-scale in-memory processing without requiring multi-node cluster distribution. The instance does not provision bundled local storage or dedicated GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached storage infrastructure for persistent data operations. Qualitative cost efficiency is realized through vertical consolidation of monolithic, RAM-heavy environments, minimizing node management complexity and clustering overheads. The m4-ultramem-112 is suited for large in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, massive caching layers, extensive data warehousing architectures, and memory-bound transactional database workloads.
